title: Paper Towels 6-roll

drivers.name: Holiday: Labor Day
drivers.evidence: Noise-adjusted multiplier x0.53 vs baseline in 2025; 2024 spike was confounded by promotion; one clean historical occurrence.

adjustment.analysis: Labor Day is a known demand driver with a noise-adjusted historical effect of x0.53 vs baseline (2025), though 2024 showed a spike (x2.12) due to a concurrent promotion. This week has no promotion (price unchanged at $9.88), so the 2025 pattern is more relevant. The classical model's x0.53 is well-supported by one clean historical example. No other drivers (e.g., price, season) apply. No evidence of pantry loading (no prior promotion). The effect is consistent with past behavior and the baseline is already adjusted for trend and seasonality.

  shelf price: 9.88 (+0.0% vs regular price 9.88)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 103.8 | 5%-95%: 68.1 - 242.5 | 10%-90%: 73.0 - 207.2

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-24% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
